expectations.text: The given technical details appear in the diagram (messages or notes): POST /v1/password-resets, 202 Accepted, 429 with Retry-After, reset_requested event via RabbitMQ, SendGrid POST /v3/mail/send with Authorization: Bearer
expectations.evidence: All inside the mermaid block: `W->>+A: POST /v1/password-resets` (line 15); `A-->>W: 202 Accepted` (line 27); `A-->>W: 429 Too Many Requests` (line 19) followed by `Note over W,A: Retry-After: ...` (line 20); `A-)Q: publish reset_requested` / `Q-)N: reset_requested consumed` with Q declared as `participant Q as RabbitMQ` (lines 10, 25, 34); `N->>S: POST /v3/mail/send` with S declared as SendGrid and `Note over N,S: Authorization: Bearer ...` (lines 12, 35-36). The request body `{ "email": "..." }` and the 5/hour/IP limit are in the note on line 16.

expectations.text: The rate-limit case is shown as a distinct branch (alt/else, break, or opt)
expectations.evidence: Line 18 `alt more than 5 requests/hour from this IP` contains the 429 reply and Retry-After note; line 21 `else within rate limit` contains the lookup/publish/202 path. Mutually exclusive branches of one alt.

expectations.text: The always-202 anti-enumeration behavior is represented (202 returned regardless of user existence)
expectations.evidence:
In the `else within rate limit` branch, after the lookup (`A->>+D: Look up user by email` / `D-->>-A: user row, or no row`) the only conditional is `opt user exists` around the publish (lines 24-26); `A-->>W: 202 Accepted` (line 27) sits outside that opt, so it happens for both lookup outcomes, and the note on line 28 reads `Always 202, whether or not the email exists,
so attackers cannot enumerate emails`.

expectations.text: The human user is declared as an actor and the event publish/consume legs are drawn with async arrows (-)) rather than sync request arrows
expectations.evidence: Line 6 `actor U as User`. The two `-)` arrows are exactly the publish and consume legs: `A-)Q: publish reset_requested` (line 25) and `Q-)N: reset_requested consumed` (line 34). All HTTP calls and the DB lookup use sync `->>`.

expectations.text: No technical details beyond what the prompt established are presented as facts (no invented endpoints, headers, TTLs, or payload fields)
expectations.evidence: Every endpoint, header, status, payload field and event name in the block traces to the prompt; the unspecified Retry-After value is left as `...` (line 20); no token TTL, reset link, token field or SendGrid response code appears. `429 Too Many Requests` is the standard reason phrase for the status the prompt gave. The run explicitly declined to draw web-app replies to the user and the SendGrid response because the prompt did not give them (lines 44-47), and discloses the publish-before-202 ordering as its own choice (line 49). The only inaccuracy is a self-referential label, `opt user exists (asynchronous, after step 8)` on line 33, which should read step 7 (see claims); it is not an invented technical fact about the system.

claims.claim: It uses only core Mermaid syntax, so GitLab's bundled renderer handles it
claims.evidence:
Block uses sequenceDiagram, autonumber, actor/participant, ->>/-->>/-), +/- activation, alt/else/opt, Note over with
, and %% comments; nothing version-gated.

claims.claim: Opt label `(asynchronous, after step 8)` and comment `only happens when step 6 published the event`; prose: steps 1-2 submit/POST, step 3 rate limit, 4-5 lookup, 6 publish, 7 202, 8-9 async tail, swap 6 and 7 to reorder
claims.evidence: With autonumber the arrows number 1 U->>W, 2 W->>A, 3 429, 4 lookup, 5 DB reply, 6 A-)Q, 7 202, 8 Q-)N, 9 N->>S. The prose and the `%%` comment are correct, but the opt label on line 33 says the tail comes 'after step 8' when step 8 is the first arrow inside that very block; it should say 'after step 7'. Minor internal inconsistency that would ship into the wiki.

claims.evidence: The prompt does not describe either; the diagram has no W-->>U arrows and no S-->>N arrow. Consistent with record-don't-invent.

uncertainties: Web app replies to the user after 429/202 unspecified; omitted (disclosed).
SendGrid response and failure handling unknown; omitted (disclosed).

suggestions.reason: No assertion checks internal consistency of the diagram's own labels (step references under autonumber). This run's `after step 8` label is off by one and no assertion caught it. A generic 'labels and notes that cross-reference step numbers match the autonumbered arrows' assertion would catch this class of error.

suggestions.assertion: No technical details beyond what the prompt established are presented as facts (no invented endpoints, headers, TTLs, or payload fields)

eval_feedback.overall: All six assertions genuinely earned. The diagram is the stricter of the two on record-don't-invent, but carries one off-by-one step reference in an opt label that the assertion set does not cover.
